rows.value: Categories listed in Annex I, Part A
rows.text: Under Article 6(1) and Article 25(2), machinery categories listed in Annex I, Part A must follow module B with C, module H, or module G, and all three involve a notified body. Recital 59 supports this as the stricter, higher-risk route. The passages do not enumerate the individual Part A categories, so they are not named here.

value: EU type-examination (module B) followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C), Annex VII and Annex VIII
conformity based on full quality assurance (module H), Annex IX
conformity based on unit verification (module G), Annex X
rows.text: For machinery in a category listed in Annex I, Part A, Article 25(2) of the Machinery Regulation requires the manufacturer to apply one of three procedures: module B followed by module C, module H, or module G. Article 6(1) confirms that Part A categories fall under Article 25(2).

A safety component with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches that ensures safety functions falls under Annex I, Part A, point 5. Recital 54 supports this by stating that such systems should be included in Annex I.

rows.value: Where frequent access is envisaged (Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation)
rows.text: Under Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, interlocking movable guards shall be used for moving transmission parts where frequent access is envisaged; otherwise either fixed or interlocking movable guards may be used. The corresponding Directive text in Annex I, point 1.3.8.1 says "should" rather than "shall", so it is less mandatory.

The passages do not include the text of essential health and safety requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III. They contain only the Annex III section heading (1), points 1.3.3 (falling or ejected objects) and 1.5.13 (hazardous emissions), and the heading for 6.3, none of which is 1.3.7.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is considered the manufacturer.
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, a person who carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product is considered a manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations, including ensuring and declaring conformity and applying the relevant conformity assessment procedure. A non-professional user who modifies machinery for their own use is excluded. Recital 26 explains the new conformity assessment requirement.

Under the Directive, Article 5(1)(e), the EC declaration of conformity (Annex II, part 1, Section A) must accompany the machinery. Under the Regulation, Article 15(2)(b) and (c), distributors must verify that the machinery is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and by the instructions for use. Article 10(5) also allows identification information to be given in an accompanying document where the machinery's size or nature prevents marking it directly.

Manufacturers must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the product is placed on the market (Directive 2014/34/EU Art. 6(3), Directive 2014/68/EU Art. 6(3), Directive 2014/30/EU Art. 7(3), Directive 2014/35/EU Art. 6(3), Regulation (EU) 2016/425 Art. 8(3)). For machinery, Regulation Art. 10(3) requires keeping them for at least 10 years after the machinery is placed on the market or put into service.

Under Article 54 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the Regulation applies from 14 January 2027, with some earlier-dated exceptions for specific articles. The passage is labelled only 'REG, Art. 54', so the link to 2023/1230 rests on the matching article and date.

No. Under Article 52(1) of the Regulation, Member States may not impede the making available of machinery placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 14 January 2027. Since 16 January 2027 is after that cut-off, the transitional protection does not cover placing such machinery on the market on that date.

rows.value: INAIL carries out the first periodic verification, within 45 days of the employer's request according to D.Lgs. 81/2008 art. 71(11), but within 60 days according to DM 11 April 2011 art. 2(1).
rows.text: For equipment listed in Annex VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008, INAIL carries out the first periodic verification. Article 71(11) of D.Lgs. 81/2008 sets the deadline at 45 days from the request, while DM 11 April 2011, art. 2(1), sets it at 60 days. The passages do not resolve this difference, so the 45-day statutory term should be checked against the official text.

Article 5(3) of Directive 2009/104/EC requires the employer to record the results of inspections, keep them at the disposal of the authorities, and keep them for a 'suitable period of time', but it does not set a fixed duration. The Italian provision (art. 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008) requires the inspection reports to be kept and made available to the supervisory body, also without a stated period.

The passages do not include a product catalogue, any list of models, or any rule that changes conformity-assessment requirements on 20 January 2027, so they cannot show which models would need a notified body. The passages only cover general notified-body and record-keeping duties, such as the 10-year retention period in Annex IX, point 4 of Directive 2014/34/EU.

The passages do not identify model RC-5 or say when it, or any date such as 20 January 2027, takes effect. They describe general conformity assessment principles and third-party requirements for safety components and self-evolving systems, but none of them determines which procedure RC-5 needs.

The passages do not address internal production control, model CS-400, or any rule taking effect on 20 January 2027, so the question cannot be answered from them. The relevant conformity-assessment provisions would need to be checked in the full regulation text.

The passages do not contain the categories listed in Annex I, Part A of the Regulation, and the Annex IV of Directive 2006/42/EC passage is only a heading with no content. The question cannot be answered from these passages.

The passages do not support internal production control alone for vehicle servicing lifts. Annex I, Part A, point 3 lists vehicle servicing lifts, and Article 25(3) allows module A only for categories in Annex I, Part B, so Part A lifts cannot rely on it. The passages do not mention the 20 January 2027 date, so they do not confirm when this rule applies.

rows.value: Protection against corruption, covered by essential health and safety requirements in Annex III, sections 1.1.9 and 1.2.1, together with the safety and reliability of control systems
rows.text: Article 20(9) of the Regulation (REG) links protection against corruption to Annex III, sections 1.1.9 and 1.2.1, which also cover the safety and reliability of control systems. The passages do not explicitly state that the Directive 2006/42/EC lacked this requirement, so that part of the question is not confirmed by the given text.

The passages do not include a correlation table for Directive 2006/42/EC, so they do not show which Regulation article corresponds to its Article 12. The only correlation table for a Regulation (Annex X of eu-reg-2016-425) covers Directive 89/686/EEC, not 2006/42/EC.

The passages do not include a correlation table for Directive 2006/42/EC, so they do not show which Regulation annex its Annex IV corresponds to. The tables that were provided cover other directives, such as 89/686/EEC, 2004/108/EC, 2006/95/EC, 94/9/EC, and 95/16/EC.

The passages do not include Table A2, which lists the overhead travelling cranes (positions 8-13), so I cannot confirm the DEMAG crane at position 8 or its manufacture year and duty type. Passage 0 says all 24 positions follow the Allegato VII intervals, and Allegato VII sets annual verification for lifting equipment over 200 kg in the rows quoted (rows 12, 14 and 15), but which row applies depends on data not given here.

Annual verification (ogni anno), under Allegato VII, row 12 of D.Lgs. 81/08, which applies to mobile lifting equipment over 200 kg used in extractive and similar sectors. The passages do not give position 7's make, year-of-use details, or last verification date. Its mining-area location and the 2017 build year (under 10 years old) point to this row rather than the biennial row for non-extractive use (row 13), but the passages do not state the sector explicitly for position 7.

The passages do not say who carries out periodic verifications after the first one on equipment listed in Annex VII. Annex VII of the Machinery Regulation, as quoted in passage 6, covers EU type-examination by a notified body, and no passage describes periodic re-verification.

Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 requires INAIL to carry out the first periodic verification within forty-five days of the request, and that is the figure I'd rely on. Article 2(1) of the 2011 Ministerial Decree says sixty days, which conflicts with the statute it cites, so the discrepancy should be checked before relying on either number. Today's date (2026-11-14) does not affect the calculation.

The passages do not directly say whether the UR5e may be put into service on its own as delivered. Section 6 (Assembly and Mounting, p. 38) states that the robot arm, Control Box and Teach Pendant must be assembled before you can continue, and section 4.1 (p. 30) says system design and installation are not covered there and that the assembly instructions must be followed. Section 4.4 (Integration and Responsibility) is listed in the contents but its text is not included.

The nanoScan3 must be tested at least once a year: the regular thorough check (Section 5.6.2, page 50, and the minimum requirements on page 51) includes the principal function check and the detection capability (resolution) test. Daily checks of the visual inspection and principal function are only recommended, not required.

Under the verifier's commitments in the IGEA technical specification (Scheda Tecnica, section 4, p. 5), when planning the inspections jointly with IGEA's appointed staff, the verifier must notify IGEA at least 15 days in advance.

Position 13 (IGEA-PRIM 5t overhead travelling crane, built 2017) falls under the Allegato VII D.Lgs. 81/08 lifting-equipment entry for non-hand-operated appliances over 200 kg, which requires verification every year. The passages do not explicitly classify an overhead travelling crane under that entry, so this is an inference from the category.

In November 2028 the IGEA-PRIM crane (position 13, built 2017) will be more than 10 years old, so under Allegato VII row 14 it falls in the 'older than 10 years' category and must be verified annually, not biennially as under row 13.

The passages place the platform at position 24 (table A6) and say its periodic verification follows the intervals in Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08, but they do not give the interval for elevating platforms. The Allegato VII rows provided cover pressure equipment and piping, not lifting equipment, and table A6 with the HINOWA entry is not included.

The passages do not give the last verification date for the DEMAG overhead crane at position 8, which is listed in Table A2 of Allegato A (positions 8-13, 'gru a ponte scorrevole'). Without that date, it cannot be determined whether the verification is overdue today (2026-11-14). Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 sets annual cadences for some lifting equipment, but the passages do not confirm that this crane falls under that row.
Replacing the UR5e (reach 850 mm, passage 7) with the UR10e (reach 1300 mm, passage 4) increases the reach by 450 mm, from the Technical Specifications in section 3.1 of each manual.
The load nut's wear indicator on the MA STAR 3.5 A must be checked every 6 months, as stated in section 7.3 of the MA STAR manual (p. 34).

The passages do not show the IGEA list entry for position 8 (the DEMAG overhead crane) or its age. Article 5 of the IGEA technical sheet requires a structural verification certificate for residual life cycles only if the equipment is over 20 years old, so the answer depends on the crane's age, which is not given.
